newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITSUBISHI MOTORS BOOSTS STAKE IN THAI VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: MITSUBISHI MOTORS BOOSTS STAKE IN THAI VENTURE.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Thursday it has paid about 22 billion yen to boost its stake in its Thai joint venture, MMC Sittipol Co, to 98 percent from 48 percent.
The subsidiary, which currently makes commercial vehicles, may begin producing new models in future for export, a spokesman for Mitsubishi Motors said.
The spokesman said the Thai subsidiary has a high level of international competitiveness from a medium- to long-term standpoint, despite Thailand's recent foreign exchange turmoil.

On Tuesday, Thailand, in deep recession as a result of the collapse of a real estate and asset "bubble", announced a series of economic reform measures and said it was seeking the loans from foreign countries and the International Monetary Fund to stabilise its economy.
The economic problems in Thailand have prompted other Japanese companies to take a cautious stance on investments there.
Mitsubishi Motors more than doubled the capital of the Thai firm to three billion yen and bought about 90 percent of the 52 percent stake a local business group had held in the joint venture.
The Thai firm produced about 87,000 vehicles, mainly pickup trucks, in the year ended in March 1997.
